scope: Categories describe mechanisms and evidence coverage, not a promise that every attack in a category is detected. Labels are research metadata, never model inputs.

main_review.distinction: Main groups evaluations by protocol type; re-entry, flash loans and value flows are separate card features. Protocol type is not an exploit root cause. EVM transactions and accuracy numbers are not transferred to NEAR.

transferred_methods.near_evidence: Exact token-unit deposits, refunds and surviving credit from authenticated receipt emitters
transferred_methods.limit: Event accounting is not a historical balance proof or USD-valued protocol solvency check.

transferred_methods.near_evidence: Earlier receipt-backed participant activity; chronological, bounded and deduplicated
transferred_methods.limit: Shared relayers and later transactions must not become attacker labels or predictive identity features.
NEAR receipt ancestry is not the synchronous EVM call stack; a callback is not reentrancy evidence by itself.

transferred_methods.near_evidence: Legitimate withdrawals, refunds, failed deposits and authorized administration
transferred_methods.limit: An outflow or failed call alone does not prove an exploit.

transferred_methods.near_evidence: Hold out incident/actor/template groups within families and entire families
transferred_methods.limit: Randomized copies of one exploit are not independent incidents.

observability.supported: The detector has a specific receipt-pattern check for part of this category; this is not full-category coverage.
observability.detectable_with_context: Requires additional authenticated protocol state or authorization semantics; generic receipt shape is insufficient.
observability.not_observable: The current Intents receipt detector does not validate the required external-chain evidence.

families.label: Callback accounting
families.evm_analogue: Unbacked mint, double refund, broken balance accounting
families.near_mechanism: A deposit leaves internal credit after the backing token is refunded, or a failed callback skips reconciliation.
families.checked_scope: Matched successful Intents deposit, token refund and credit events, with complete receipt ancestry.

families.label: Async state race
families.near_mechanism: Another call uses stale or prematurely credited state before a callback settles an earlier operation.
families.checked_scope: A suspicious history sequence is a clue; proving a race needs ordered interleaving and protocol state.

families.label: Access-control probe
families.evm_analogue: Missing access control, tx.origin misuse, unauthorized upgrade
families.near_mechanism: An outsider calls a private callback or administrative method; signer and immediate predecessor are different identities.
families.checked_scope: Direct private/admin call patterns and repeated rejected probes. A rejected call is an attempt, not a successful privilege bypass.
requires: role state to establish successful unauthorized access

families.label: Token or receiver spoofing
families.evm_analogue: Fake-token deposits and forged receiver callbacks
families.near_mechanism: An untrusted token or caller supplies false deposit claims or impersonates a token receiver callback.
families.checked_scope: Some direct receiver probes are visible; token authenticity and economic backing require a protocol-specific registry or state proof.

families.label: Callback resource exhaustion
families.evm_analogue: Gas griefing and denial of service
families.near_mechanism: Gas, log or returned-value limits interrupt a callback; storage growth can also consume protocol funds.
families.checked_scope: Receipt gas/log/value-limit failures. Intentional griefing and storage-cost abuse are not established by failure alone.

families.label: Replay or signature authorization
families.evm_analogue: Permit replay, signature forgery and authorization theft
families.near_mechanism: A reused nonce, wrong verifying contract, expired intent or unauthorized key is accepted.
families.checked_scope: The current detector does not independently verify signatures, historical nonce state or key authority.

families.label: Oracle or price manipulation
families.evm_analogue: Oracle manipulation and flash-loan-assisted economic attacks
families.near_mechanism: A protocol accepts manipulated or stale prices and transfers excessive value.
families.checked_scope: A large transfer, swap or loan is not sufficient; no generic price-abuse rule is claimed.

families.label: Arithmetic or rounding
families.evm_analogue: Overflow, precision loss and rounding exploitation
families.near_mechanism: Protocol arithmetic awards more assets or claims than its state transition permits.
families.checked_scope: A receipt discrepancy can expose an effect, but cannot identify an arithmetic bug without protocol math and state.

families.label: Share or claim accounting
families.evm_analogue: Vault donation, share inflation and excess redemption
families.near_mechanism: A withdrawal pays more than the burned shares, claims or internal balance authorize.
families.checked_scope: Legitimate withdrawals must include surrendered claims and exchange rates; the current deposit check is not a vault adapter.

families.label: Protocol accounting logic
families.evm_analogue: Business-logic accounting and circular-route output inflation
families.near_mechanism: A protocol counts intermediate or reused assets as final output and accepts an underbacked position.
families.checked_scope: Rhea is a sourced external-protocol example; the Intents deposit checker does not validate its margin solvency.

families.label: Bridge message validation
families.evm_analogue: Forged bridge messages and duplicate bridge claims
families.near_mechanism: A bridge accepts an invalid source-chain proof or processes the same external claim twice.
families.checked_scope: Receiving bridged tokens in Intents does not prove that their source-chain backing or bridge proof was valid.

inference_note: Mappings to price, arithmetic, share and bridge categories are engineering generalizations of the reviewed main-branch mechanisms, not claims of a demonstrated NEAR Intents vulnerability.
